rationale: Bubblesort is a tiny benchmark consisting of one or two hot-loop functions dominated by array loads/stores, comparisons, and swaps, so cheap arithmetic and data-flow transforms should dominate: SUB gets high SecurityGain/DiversityGain weights with low cost weights because instruction substitution obscures the swap/comparison idioms at near-zero runtime and size overhead, and SPLIT gets a high DiversityGain weight since splitting its few basic blocks multiplies variant diversity cheaply. BCF and FLA are weighted heavily on RuntimeCost/SizeCost/CorrectnessRisk because their dispatcher and bogus-block machinery lands directly inside the hot sort loop where every iteration pays the tax; keeping those weights high makes the selector apply them selectively (e.g., only to the outer loop driver) rather than uniformly. FLA's CorrectnessRisk weight is kept high since flattening loop-carry dependencies (the sorted-scan flag) is where semantic breakage is most likely in this program. IBR gets moderate weights as a mid-cost mid-gain option, while ICALL is near-disabled (low SecurityGain, high RuntimeCost and CorrectnessRisk) because Bubblesort has essentially no indirect-call sites to hide and any call indirection would be pure overhead; IGV is similarly restrained since its only real target is the array/loop-bound globals, which are few, making its marginal security payoff small relative to the per-access indirection cost paid on every inner-loop iteration.
